title.en: Kinetic energy and the work-energy theorem

body.en: *Kinetic energy* is $K = \tfrac12 mv^2$, the energy a body has because of its motion. The work-energy theorem says the work done by the net force on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy: $W_{net} = K_f - K_i$. It follows from $v^2 - u^2 = 2as$ multiplied by m/2.
body.kn: ಚಲನ ಶಕ್ತಿ K = ½mv², ಚಲನೆಯಿಂದ ಕಾಯಕ್ಕಿರುವ ಶಕ್ತಿ. ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಲ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸವು ಚಲನ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗೆ ಸಮ: W = K_f − K_i. ಇದೇ ಕೆಲಸ-ಶಕ್ತಿ ಪ್ರಮೇಯ.

say.en: K equals p squared/2 metres.
Doubling v makes K four times.
Start from v squared minus u squared equals 2 a s and multiply by m over 2.
The net work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.
When the force changes with position, the work is the area under the force–position graph.
For F equal to 4 x plus 5, from 1 to 4 metres, the area is 45 joules.
Example: a 1000 kilogram car at 20 metres per second stops in 40 metres. The braking force follows from the change in kinetic energy.

title.en: Work done by a variable force

body.en: When the force changes with position, split the path into tiny steps and add up the work: $W = \int_{x_i}^{x_f} F(x)\,dx$. This equals the area under the force–displacement graph. The work-energy theorem holds for *variable forces* too.
body.kn: ಬಲವು ಸ್ಥಾನದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಬದಲಾದರೆ W = ∫F dx. ಇದು ಬಲ–ಸ್ಥಾನಪಲ್ಲಟ ನಕ್ಷೆಯ ಅಡಿಯ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಫಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮ. ಕೆಲಸ-ಶಕ್ತಿ ಪ್ರಮೇಯ ಬದಲಾಗುವ ಬಲಕ್ಕೂ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Area under the F–x graph = work
Area below the x-axis counts as negative work

heading.en: Work, Kinetic Energy and the Work–Energy Theorem

tagline.en: The scalar product, work done by a constant force, kinetic energy, the work–energy theorem and work done by a variable force as the area under a force–displacement graph.

myth.en: A coolie carrying a heavy box on his head along a level platform does a lot of work on the box against gravity.

truth.en: Gravity (and the upward support force) act vertically while the box moves horizontally, so θ = 90° and the work done by each on the box is zero. He feels tired, because his muscles use energy internally, and in everyday speech that is 'work'. In physics, work needs a displacement with a component along the force.

say.en: $\vec A \cdot \vec B = AB\cos\theta = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z$.
Work $W = Fd\cos\theta$: positive, zero or negative depending on θ. Unit: joule.
Kinetic energy $K = \tfrac12 mv^2 = p^2/(2m)$.
Work–energy theorem: $W_{\text{net}} = K_f - K_i$, for constant and variable forces.
Work by a variable force = area under the F–x graph.

goal.en: The scalar product, work done by a constant force, kinetic energy, the work–energy theorem and work done by a variable force as the area under a force–displacement graph.

question.en: A block slides on a rough floor and comes to rest. The work done on it by kinetic friction is:

explain.en: Friction points opposite to the displacement (θ = 180°), so its work is negative and the kinetic energy falls.

task.en: Is the work done by the named force positive, negative or zero?

explain.en: Look at the angle between the force and the displacement: less than 90° gives positive work, more than 90° gives negative work, exactly 90° gives zero.

takeaway.en: $\vec A \cdot \vec B = AB\cos\theta = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z$.

narration.en: Many people think: A coolie carrying a heavy box on his head along a level platform does a lot of work on the box against gravity. Actually: Gravity (and the upward support force) act vertically while the box moves horizontally, so θ = 90° and the work done by each on the box is zero. He feels tired, because his muscles use energy internally, and in everyday speech that is 'work'. In physics, work needs a displacement with a component along the force.

problem.en: A net force acts on a 2 kg ball moving at 3 m/s until its speed is 5 m/s. Find the work done by the net force.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A net force acts on a 2 kg ball moving at 3 m/s until its speed is 5 m/s. Find the work done by the net force.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A net force acts on a 2 kilograms ball moving at 3 metres per second until its speed is 5 metres per second. Find the work done by the net force.
K i equals one half times 2 times 9 equals 9 joules; K f equals one half times 2 times 25 equals 25 joules.
W equals K f - K i equals 16 joules.
So the answer is 16 joules.

problem.en: A force F = 3x² N acts on a particle along the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 2 m. Find the work done.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A force F = 3x² N acts on a particle along the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 2 m. Find the work done.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A force F equals 3x squared N acts on a particle along the x-axis from x equals 0 to x equals 2 metres. Find the work done.
W equals the integral of 0 squared 3x squared dx = [x cubed] 0 squared.
W equals 8 minus 0 equals 8 joules.
So the answer is 8 joules.

body.en: K = p²/2m. For equal momenta, the lighter body has more kinetic energy. For equal kinetic energies, the heavier body has more momentum, since p = √(2mK).
